subject: Model fit benchmarks + Redwood-verified performance profiles
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: model fit discovery + next steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Nice to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Objective: Evaluate a small set of candidate models on your fraud-detection prompt set (short text + structured metadata) to validate accuracy and latency at your target TPS.
- Recommended next steps: 1) Share a ~1000-sample prompt set (anonymized) for a scoped eval; 2) Redwood runs a benchmark with both full-precision and quantized variants; 3) Review results and pick a model for a 2-week pilot on Dedicated capacity.

I attached a sample prompt set and our standard benchmark PDF so you have context. I'll have Marissa follow up with the verified performance profiles we referenced (TPS numbers, p50/p95 latencies).

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the target steady-state TPS (requests/sec) and your max acceptable p95 latency?
- Any data residency or VPC requirements we should flag now?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai

Thanks Alex — this looks good. Quick answers:

- Target TPS: 35 steady-state, with short bursts to ~80 for peak windows.
- Max acceptable p95 latency: 300 ms end-to-end for our interactive tooling.
- Data residency: US-only for production; evals can run on hosted infra in us-west.

We'll anonymize and share a 1k sample offline by EOD Friday. Also curious about your benchmark metrics: are the TPS numbers you shared measured for single-instance Dedicated configs or for auto-scaled Hosted?

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, FinTechCo

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-03T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit discovery + next steps

Samir —

Thanks for the answers. Short answers re: benchmarks: our Redwood-verified performance profiles are published per model variant and include both single-instance Dedicated numbers (baseline throughput at target batch sizes) and scaled-hosted numbers (measured on our hosted pool with autoscaling). The benchmark PDF I attached gives example configs; the live link below will show the exact test harness and hardware.

To make this concrete, here are initial model recommendations based on what we discussed:

- redwood-2-7B-quant (Q4_8): best cost/latency balance for short structured prompts; in our evals it achieves ~45 TPS on a single r5g.2x-type Dedicated GPU equivalent with p50=28ms, p95=120ms for 256-token context.
- llama-3-8b-q4: slightly higher quality on few-shot prompts but ~30% slower on tail latencies; expect ~30 TPS, p95 ~180ms in similar config.
- redwood-7b-ht (fp16): when accuracy is prioritized and you have Dedicated capacity, expect p95 ~95ms but higher cost.

Action items I suggest:
1) You share the anonymized prompt set.
2) We run two benchmark passes: (A) Redwood-hosted baseline; (B) Dedicated single-instance with your target batch settings. We'll produce TPS curves, latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95), and quality comparison vs your labeled eval samples.
3) If you have a small labeled validation set (100-200 labeled cases), we can include quality regression checks and per-prompt failure analysis.

I've uploaded the per-model performance profile CSVs to the drive link. Marissa — can you add the standard quality-regression checklist and the prompt-eval pipeline notes to the Drive folder?

Thanks,
Alex

Attachments referenced: redwood_benchmarks_q2.pdf
Related link: https://redwood-inference.app/benchmarks/FIN-2026-034

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechco.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-05T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit discovery + next steps

Hi Samir — following up with the model profiles and a couple of notes from our ML ops side. Summary of verified perf (from our Q2 harness) that are relevant to your workload: 

- redwood-2-7B-quant (q4_8):
  - Throughput (single-instance measured with continuous batching): 45 TPS (256 token context)
  - Latency percentiles: p50=28ms, p90=85ms, p95=120ms
  - Cost: lowest among tested FP/quant combos; recommended first pass for production.

- llama-3-8b-q4:
  - Throughput: 30 TPS
  - Latency percentiles: p50=45ms, p90=150ms, p95=180ms
  - Notes: higher few-shot QA quality in our internal evals on instruction-rich prompts; watch out for hallucination cases on structured anomaly descriptions.

- redwood-7b-ht (fp16):
  - Throughput: 22 TPS
  - Latency percentiles: p50=25ms, p90=70ms, p95=95ms
  - Notes: better deterministic outputs for structured templates but higher GPU cost.

Quality/regression concerns and mitigations:
- If you use quantized variants, we recommend a targeted quality check on critical prompts (10-20% of your samples) to validate there is no unacceptable regression. We'll run automated diff checks against the labeled set and flag any delta in precision/recall metrics.
- For bursts to ~80 TPS: recommend a small burst capacity policy on Dedicated or a fallback model (cheaper variant) in Hosted to prevent degradation during autoscaling warm-up.

Links and artifacts I've added to the shared Drive folder:
- redwood_perf_profiles_FIN-2026-034.csv
- prompt_evaluation_notebook.ipynb
- quality_regression_checklist.md

Next steps: once we have your anonymized prompt set, we'll run the benchmark (2-3 business days) and post a results summary in the Drive + HubSpot deal record. If you'd like, we can also schedule a 30-min walk-through of the benchmark output with our ML team.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments uploaded to Drive: redwood_perf_profiles_FIN-2026-034.csv, quality_regression_checklist.md
